### Problem description

After upgrading the Termux x11/sfml package to 3.1.0, my SFML program fails to start with a runtime linker error:

> CANNOT LINK EXECUTABLE "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/projects/water-simulation-cpp/build/release/WaterWaves": cannot locate symbol "_ZN2sf4priv11getActivityEv" referenced by "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/libsfml-window.so"...

The same project works with SFML 3.0.2.

1. Install SFML from the Termux X11 repo:
   pkg install x11-repo sfml clang cmake.

### Problem description

Tab Crashes in Browsers based on Firefox >= v151.0  
  
Starting with the upgrade to Firefox v151.0, when trying to load https://duckduckgo.com or https://duck.ai the tab crashes every time. This is true for the versions Librewolf and Zen Browser based on Firefox v151 as well. Chromium can load these pages normally. As a sanity check, I tried loading these pages with Firefox v151.0.1,2 on FreeBSD and the pages load normally. These two sites are the only ones that I've found to have this issue under Termux so far.  
  
In Firefox, I disabled all extensions but the issue persists.  If this issue is unique to me, that is extra puzzling. I tried to do a debug build of Firefox, but my little build host was brought to it's knees and the build was killed, so I don't have any useful debugging output at this time.

payload.body: ### Problem description Hi, since I did not get answer related to this issue in the Termux Discord server, I decided to open an issue here. There are 2 issues. Firstly, some functions in `code-oss` (like cloning the repo) doesn't work. I use it but nothing happens. I can't find error logs for that either. Secondly, I saw some **undeletable** files in my home directory, with random unknown characters. There's also some logs related to it. ### Problem description


While installing/upgrading python and python-pip in Termux, the installation prints the following traceback during setup:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/py3compile", line 323, in <module>
    main()
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/py3compile", line 284, in main
    pkg_files = tuple(dpf.from_package(options.package))
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.13/debpython/files.py", line 68, in from_package
    raise Exception("cannot get content of %s" % package_name)
Exception: cannot get content of python

A similar traceback also appears for "python-pip" and "proot-distro".

However, after installation:

- "python --version" works
- "pip --version" works
- Python itself appears functional

This may be an issue with package metadata or post-install scripts for Python 3.13 packages.

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Install the latest version of stable termux 0.118.3
Then run: apt update; apt upgrade -y
Then: apt install python

### What is the expected behavior?

The python and python-pip packages should install/reinstall without throwing traceback errors during the post-install step ("py3compile").

- Installation completes cleanly
- No "Exception: cannot get content of python" errors appear
- Post-install scripts execute successfully

### Why is it worth to add this package?

### Package Name
antigravity-cli (or `agy`)

### Package Description
Google has deprecated `gemini-cli` (npm package) and transitioned to the new native binary format known as 'Antigravity CLI' (`agy`). It is an AI-powered agentic command-line interface tool used to interact with Google AI Pro/Ultra models, local artifacts, and file systems.

### Home Page / Source Code URL
https://developers.googleblog.com/build-with-google-antigravity-our-new-agentic-development-platform/

### Is the package compiled or pure script?
Compiled (Pre-built native binaries are currently distributed by Google for Linux, macOS, and Windows, but lack native Android/Termux environment targets).

### Additional Context / Reason for Request
The old Node.js-based `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` workflow is officially scheduled to stop serving API requests on June 18, 2026. Developers using Termux for mobile coding workflows currently have to rely on heavy `proot-distro` Linux layers just to run the pre-compiled x86/ARM Linux `agy` binary. 

Having a native Termux package (or build-from-source patches) for `antigravity-cli` would keep native Android AI workflows functional past the 2026 deprecation deadline.


### Home page URL

_No response_

### Source code URL

https://storage.googleapis.com/antigravity-public/antigravity-hub/2.0.1-6566078776737792/linux-arm/Antigravity.tar.gz

### Packaging policy acknowledgement

- [ ] The project is actively developed.
- [ ] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [ ] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [ ] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [ ] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

### Additional information

payload.author: pcosway
payload.body:
### Problem description

This is a duplicate of https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/2743#issuecomment-4480487966
Posted here in case it is more appropriate to fix in termux-packages than the main psutil code.

Another Android/Termux issue -- I have some older Android devices where /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_max_freq is not readable.

Thus, this line in \_pslinux.py does not work correctly.
max_ = int(bcat(pjoin(path, "scaling_max_freq"))) / 1000

For my purposes, I made a change that seems to work -- but I don't know if that is a good general change!

```          
            try:
                max_ = int(bcat(pjoin(path, "scaling_max_freq"))) / 1000
            except (PermissionError):
                # in case scaling_max_freq is not readable
                max_ = int(bcat(pjoin(path, "cpuinfo_max_freq"))) / 1000
```

I discovered it running s-tui.   Instead of getting useful information, I received an error message, ending with:

s-tui would work as expected

payload.body:
### Why is it worth to add this package?

Like https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/packages/rust/rust-std-wasm32-unknown-unknown.subpackage.sh but `rust-std-wasm32v1-none`
https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support/wasm32v1-none.html

Use case: what if you want to write smart contracts on your phone or develop for the Polkadot SDK? Many blockchains, such as Polkadot, Stellar Soroban, and others, use the `wasm32v1-none` target to build their WASM modules (they are very minimal and don't contain any new WASM instructions). As far as I understand, `wasm32v1-none` is `#![no_std]`, so it seems like perhaps the package should be called `rust-core-wasm32v1-none`?

```
$ pwd
~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/wasm32v1-none
$ tree
.
└── lib
    ├── liballoc-a50fd34f052dadc8.rlib
    ├── liballoc-a50fd34f052dadc8.rmeta
    ├── libcompiler_builtins-cfed45b7e1ab63be.rlib
    ├── libcompiler_builtins-cfed45b7e1ab63be.rmeta
    ├── libcore-369ac56680d5ca06.rlib
    └── libcore-369ac56680d5ca06.rmeta

2 directories, 6 files
$ du -sh
54M	.
```

Need to add a few of these `rlib` files so you can use `alloc`, `core` and `compiler_builtins` pre-built for `wasm32v1-none`

The $PREFIX/lib/libliquid.so.1 symlink is created.

N/A Packaging bug.

<https://www.alifevirtual.com/download.php> uses *Firestorm Viewer* not just to explore, but also to produce, worlds.

- [x] The project is actively developed.
- [x] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [x] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [x] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [x] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

<https://github.com/FirestormViewer/phoenix-firestorm/blob/master/doc/building_linux.md> says how to build the source code into *Unix* executables.

### Problem description

It's not possible to use the polyc script (insalled through `pkg install polyml`) tocompile programs, because `ld` can't find the `libpolymain` library which is available when installing PolyML on Linpx.

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

1. pkg install polyml
2. echo "fun main () = print (Int.toString 1)" > print_1.sml
3. polyc print_1.sml

The third commad invoking `polyc` fails because the `polymain` normally insalled along with PolyML library cannot be found by `ld`.

### What is the expected behavior?

It should compile find and find the required library, like on non-Android environmets.

### Why is it worth to add this package?

This is a Beancount-compatible implementation in Rust. Extremely fast.

### Home page URL

https://rustledger.github.io/

### Source code URL

https://github.com/rustledger/rustledger

### Packaging policy acknowledgement

- [x] The project is actively developed.
- [x] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [x] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [x] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [ ] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

### Additional information

Cargo binstall seems broken in Termux.
Cargo install fails due to stack overflow while compiling cranelift.
```
cargo install rustledger --no-default-features --features bean-compat
```
works as an alternative. It skips the WASM plugin support. However, the compilation on a phone is a bit painful. This prevents adding plugins, though.
